Best 500. Launch Catalogue

The 500 best keywords, picked for high returns at low cost. Keywords that run in several countries are grouped into one line. Tags mark the cheapest, highest return picks.

Recommended OEM Ontology

The Best 500 organised as a tree: portfolio → asset class (campaign) → value cluster (ad group) → keyword. This mirrors the account structure we recommend building in Google Ads, following the multi-level keyword optimisation framework (Yang et al. 2022) and keyword targeting research (Li & Yang 2022).

Best 300. Scale-Up Catalogue

The research-backed expansion set: the top 300 keywords selected from the full universe using a composite score that combines ROI tier, relevance to MultiBank's business, and search volume — the selection logic recommended in the academic literature on keyword targeting and ROI-constrained bidding (see the Research Basis tab).

How the 300 were chosen

Composite score = 40% ROI tier + 25% business relevance + 20% purchase intent + 15% search volume (log-scaled). Before scoring, keywords are de-duplicated per country and two research-mandated filters are applied: competitor / third-party brand terms are excluded (per the Chairman’s instruction and because such traffic is non-incremental — Gordon et al. 2023), and news / quote-checking / education-only queries are removed or heavily penalised (Ouyang et al. 2025: high cost of conversion, low ad relevance). ROI tier carries the largest weight per ROI-constrained autobidding (Balseiro et al. 2023); intent and relevance follow the joint selection logic of Li & Yang (2022); volume is deliberately the smallest factor because raw volume is a poor proxy for incremental value.

Why These 300. Keyword-by-Keyword Justification

Every keyword in the Best 300 with a one-line reason for inclusion and a clickable research grouping — each pill links straight to the paper that justifies it. MultiBank-relevant terms are ranked first. Use the download button to hand the Chairman the full list as a spreadsheet.

#KeywordAssetCountryVolume / moROI TierResearch GroupWhy it's in the 300

Best 300. Ontology Taxonomy

The Best 300 organised as a research-driven taxonomy: research group (each linked to its paper) → asset class → keyword, with the one-line justification under every keyword. This is the structure to present to the Chairman: every branch of the tree traces back to a peer-reviewed source.

Research Basis

Every selection rule in this dashboard is grounded in peer-reviewed research on paid-search keyword optimisation, true ROI measurement, and ROI-constrained bidding — in line with the Chairman's brief (see the Chairman Email button above). Below: the papers and how each one is applied.

The Evidence Behind the List

Seven peer-reviewed and working papers that back the three decisions in this programme: no brand terms, cheapest viable cost per click, and how we intend to prove the return. Every result below is quoted from the paper, and every link resolves.

Should we drop brand keywords?
Yes, but hold a defensive test
Brand ads showed no measurable short-term lift in the eBay experiments. The counter-evidence is that generic spend manufactures branded demand, so run one geo holdout before going to zero.
Can cheap keywords carry high return?
Yes, and the effect is measurable
Cost per conversion and conversion rate are negatively correlated across industries. Low CPC does not imply low quality, and the optimiser finds high-profit low-cost terms deliberately.
How do we prove the ROI?
Geo holdouts, not modelling
With 663 experiments and 5,000+ user features, neither double machine learning nor propensity matching recovered the experimental answer. Account data alone will not tell us what worked.

Selecting the keywords

3 papers

Why an optimiser looks for low-cost terms on purpose, and why a human still reviews the AI-generated list keyword by keyword.

Yanwu Yang
School of Management, HUST · with Huiran Li, Shanghai Customs College
Searches the whole targeting space to find high-profit, low-cost keywords with the right match type. Beat 7 baselines on profit, and the margin widened as budget grew.
Keyword Targeting Optimization in Sponsored Search Advertising: Combining Selection and Matching
Electronic Commerce Research & Applications 2022
arXiv PDFJournal
Yanwu Yang
School of Management, Huazhong University of Science & Technology
Optimises keywords at market, campaign and adgroup level together. Outperformed 2 strategies in common agency practice across two real campaign datasets.
Keyword Optimization in Sponsored Search Advertising: A Multi-Level Computational Framework
Working paper 2022
arXiv PDFScholar
Martin Reisenbichler
WU Vienna University of Economics and Business
Two field tests in a cost-per-click setup. LLMs on their own were not sufficient; the best performance came from a hybrid with human judgment applied at the individual keyword level.
Applying Large Language Models to Sponsored Search Advertising
Marketing Science 45(1) 2026
JournalFree PDF

Proving the return

4 papers

Why the account dashboard cannot answer “did this work”, and what does.

Brett R. Gordon
Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University
Analysed 663 large-scale experiments with 5,000+ user-level features. Neither double machine learning nor stratified propensity matching recovered the experimental effects, even with deep learning.
Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement
Marketing Science 42(4) 2023
arXiv PDF
Brett R. Gordon
Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University
The practical middle path: learns campaign-specific corrections from attributed to incremental, instead of scaling everything by one calibration ratio from a single test.
Predicted Incrementality by Experimentation (PIE) for Ad Measurement
Working paper 2023
arXiv PDF
Manlu Ouyang
NYU Stern School of Business
Documents a negative correlation between cost per conversion and conversion rate across industries, the opposite of what the standard expectation predicts, and models why a publisher may charge less for more relevant ads.
Pay More for Less Value: Cost of Conversion and Ad Relevance
Working paper · unrefereed 2025
SSRN
Brendan Lucier
Microsoft Research, Cambridge
How platform autobidders behave under a ROI target and a spend cap at the same time. Relevant because tROAS bidding now sets our impression-level bids, not our keyword list.
Autobidders with Budget and ROI Constraints: Efficiency, Regret, and Pacing Dynamics
COLT 2024 2024
arXiv PDFPMLR
Read this before quoting a figure. The three working papers are not yet peer reviewed, so treat their numbers as indicative. One widely circulated statistic is deliberately absent here: the claim that long-tail keywords convert 2.5× better than head terms comes from vendor research, not published work, so it is not cited above. The mechanism is well supported in the literature; the specific multiple is not.

Top 300 by Country

Pick a country to see its 300 strongest keywords, ranked by relevance to MultiBank's business first and value second. Countries and keywords come from the August 2026 PPC Campaign Plan.

Method. Keywords are scored the way marketing research recommends: business relevance first, then value (searches per dollar of cost). This follows Rutz, Trusov & Bucklin (2011), "Modeling Indirect Effects of Paid Search Advertising," Marketing Science 30(4), who start keyword selection from the firm's key business areas, and Rutz & Bucklin (2011), "From Generic to Branded," Journal of Marketing Research 48 on generic-term value. Cheap long-tail terms are kept because Skiera, Eckert & Hinz (2010) and the keyword-portfolio work of Symitsi et al. (2022), European Journal of Operational Research show low-cost keywords often beat expensive head terms on return.
